1.s: In 520 BC Haggai challenges the returned exiles: you live in panelled houses while God’s house lies in ruins. “Consider your ways.” Zerubbabel, Joshua and the people begin rebuilding.
1.d: The people’s panelled houses contrasted with God’s ruined temple [[tosn:Haggai 1:4]]. The key phrase is “Consider your ways” (1:5, 7) [[tbd:008:Haggai, Book of]]. “I am with you” confirms God’s presence in their building work [[tosn:Haggai 1:13]].

2.s: The new temple seems small, but God says, “The latter glory of this house will be greater than the former,” for he will shake the nations. Zerubbabel will be like God’s signet ring.
2.d: God will shake heaven and earth again; Hebrews 12:26–27 links this to Christ’s return [[tosn:Haggai 2:6–7]]. The “latter glory” may point to the Messiah coming to his temple, where Jesus was presented and taught [[tosn:Haggai 2:9]]. Zerubbabel, of David’s line, reverses the curse on Jehoiachin [[tosn:Haggai 2:21]].
